title: CVE-2026-125350: Chrome XML Zero-Day Exploited in the Wild
content_md: Google has released an emergency security update addressing CVE-2026-125350, a high-severity zero-day vulnerability in the XML component of Google Chrome that is already being exploited in real-world attacks. The issue is classified as a use-after-free memory-safety flaw and was reported anonymously to Google on November 6, 2026. Google confirmed on November 9 that an exploit for the vulnerability exists in the wild. However, the company has not disclosed how attackers are delivering the exploit, which organizations or individuals are being targeted, or whether the vulnerability is being chained with additional browser or sandbox escape flaws. Access to the underlying Chromium bug remains restricted while users deploy the security update. The fix is included in Chrome Stable 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and macOS and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. Google also released Extended Stable 156.0.8078.96 for Windows and macOS with a fix for the same vulnerability. Contact Sales CVE-2026-125350 is the eighth Chrome zero-day known to have been exploited in the wild during 2026, following CVE-2026-2441, CVE-2026-3909, CVE-2026-3910, CVE-2026-5281, CVE-2026-11645, CVE-2026-85046, and CVE-2026-87491. As of November 10, SecurityWeek reports that CISA has not yet added the newly disclosed flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
